explain: With I we always use am: I am, you are, he/she/it is. Example: I am happy.

notes.is: Is goes with he, she or it: She is a student.
notes.are: Are goes with you, we and they: You are a student.
notes.be: Be needs a helper word first: I can be a student.

explain: With he, she or it we use has, not have. Example: Tom has a cat.

notes.have: Have goes with I, you, we and they: I have two brothers.
notes.haves: There is no word 'haves'. The -s form of have is has.
notes.having: Having needs is/are first, and we don't use it for family.

explain: They takes are: we are, you are, they are. Example: They are my friends.

notes.is: Is is for one person or thing: He is from Spain.
notes.am: Am only goes with I: I am from Spain.
notes.be: Be needs a helper word: They will be in Spain.

explain: Use an before a vowel sound (a, e, i, o, u). Example: an egg, an orange.

notes.a: A goes before a consonant sound: a banana. Apple starts with a vowel.
notes.two: Two needs a plural word: two apples.
notes.many: Many needs a plural word too: many apples.

explain: We ask about a name with What. Example: What is your name? – I'm Lily.

notes.Who: Who asks about a person: Who is she? – My sister.
notes.Where: Where asks about a place: Where is your bag?
notes.When: When asks about a time: When is your birthday?

explain: With I, you, we, they the 'not' word is don't. Example: I don't like rain.

notes.doesn't: Doesn't is for he, she, it: She doesn't like coffee.
notes.not: We can't say 'I not like'. We need don't.
notes.no: No goes before a noun: I have no coffee.

explain: For things he/she/it does often, add -s to the verb. Example: She reads every day.

notes.play: Play is for I, you, we, they: We play football.
notes.playing: Playing needs is: He is playing now.
notes.is play: We don't say 'is play'. Every Sunday = present simple: plays.

q: There ___ three cats in the garden.
explain: There are for more than one thing; there is for one. Example: There are two dogs.

notes.is: There is is for one thing: There is one cat.
notes.be: Be needs a helper word: There will be three cats.

explain: On means touching the top of something. Example: The cup is on the desk.

notes.at: At is for a point or place: at school, at the door.
notes.to: To shows movement: I go to the park.
notes.from: From shows where something starts: a letter from Gran.

explain: After can, use the plain verb with no -s, no -ing and no to. Example: I can sing.

notes.swims: No -s after can: we say 'Can he swim?', not 'swims'.
notes.swimming: No -ing after can: 'Can you swimming?' is wrong.
notes.to swim: No 'to' after can: 'Can you to swim?' is wrong.

explain: These means more than one, so the noun is plural. Example: These are my socks.

notes.shoe: Shoe is just one. These needs more than one: shoes.
notes.a shoe: A shoe is one shoe. These needs a plural.

explain: Questions with you/I/we/they and a normal verb start with Do. Example: Do you like cats?

notes.Does: Does is for he, she, it: Does she like ice cream?
notes.Are: Are goes with adjectives or -ing: Are you happy?
notes.Is: Is goes with he/she/it: Is it cold?

explain: Use in with months, years and seasons. Example: in June, in winter.

notes.on: On is for days and dates: on Monday, on 5th May.
notes.at: At is for clock times: at six o'clock.

explain: Look! means it is happening now, so use is + -ing. Example: Look! It is raining.

notes.sleep: Sleep is for I/you/we/they and for habits, not now.
notes.sleeps: Sleeps is for habits: The baby sleeps a lot.
notes.are sleeping: Are is for more than one. One baby takes is.

q: This is Tom. ___ is my friend.
explain: Tom is a boy, so we use he. Example: This is Sam. He is nine.

notes.She: She is for a girl or woman.
notes.It: It is for a thing or an animal.
notes.They: They is for more than one person.

explain: Yesterday is past. The past of are is were (we were, they were). Example: We were happy.

notes.was: Was is for I, he, she, it: I was at home.
notes.is: Is is now and for one person.

q: ___ is my bag? I can't find it.
explain: Where asks about a place. Example: Where is the cat? – Under the bed.

notes.What: What asks about a thing: What is this?
notes.Who: Who asks about a person: Who is that?
notes.How: How asks about the way or feelings: How are you?

explain: With he, she, it the 'not' word is doesn't. Example: He doesn't like rain.

notes.don't: Don't is for I, you, we, they.
notes.isn't: Isn't goes with adjectives: She isn't happy. Like is a verb.
notes.not: We can't say 'She not like'. We need doesn't.

explain: Umbrella starts with a vowel sound, so we use an. Example: an ice cream.

notes.a: A is for consonant sounds: a bag, a hat.
notes.some: Some is for 'more than one' or 'a bit of': some milk.
notes.two: Two needs a plural: two umbrellas.

q: The cat is ___ the box. You can't see it!
explain: In means inside something. Example: The pencil is in my bag.

notes.on: On is on the top. Then you could see the cat!
notes.at: At is for a place point: at the door.
notes.of: Of is not used for where things are.

explain: We ask about the clock with What time. Example: What time is lunch? – At one.

notes.How many: How many asks about a number of things.
notes.What day: What day asks about Monday, Tuesday...

explain: Now means use are/is + -ing. They takes are. Example: They are playing.

notes.watch: Watch is for habits: They watch TV every day.
notes.is watching: Is is for one person. They needs are.

explain: Use at with clock times. Example: at nine o'clock, at noon.

notes.in: In is for months and years: in May.
notes.on: On is for days: on Friday.
notes.to: To shows movement, not a time.

q: This is my brother. ___ name is Leo.
explain: His shows something belongs to a boy. Example: Sam and his dog.

notes.Her: Her is for a girl: my sister and her name.
notes.He: He is the person, not 'belonging to him'. We need his.
notes.Its: Its is for a thing or an animal.

q: How ___ is your grandma? She's seventy.
explain: We ask about age with How old. Example: How old are you? – I'm eight.

notes.many: How many is for counting things.
notes.much: How much is for amounts and prices.
notes.big: How big asks about size, not age.

q: There ___ a dragon in the story.
explain: One thing takes there is. Example: There is a cat on the bed.

notes.are: Are is for more than one: There are two dragons.
notes.be: Be needs a helper word first.

q: I can ___ my name in English.
explain: After can, use the plain verb. Example: She can write.
Questions with he/she/it and a normal verb start with Does. Example: Does he like fish?

notes.Do: Do is for I, you, we, they.
notes.Is: Is goes with adjectives or -ing, not 'have'.
notes.Has: Has is not used to start this question. Say 'Does she have'.

explain: Those means more than one, so use are. Example: Those are my shoes.

notes.is: Is is for one: That is my pencil.

q: Sam was tired, ___ he went to bed.
explain: So shows a result: what happened because of it. Example: It was cold, so I wore a coat.

notes.but: But shows a surprise or difference: tired, but he played.
notes.because: Because gives the reason, not the result: He went to bed because he was tired.
notes.or: Or gives a choice: tea or milk?

explain: I/you/we/they have; he/she/it has. Example: I have a cat.

notes.am: Am is for 'I am…', not for owning things.
notes.is: Is is for he/she/it, and not for owning.

explain: He/she/it is. Example: She is kind.
We/you/they are. Example: We are happy.

notes.is: Is is for one person or thing.

explain: Questions with I/you/we/they start with Do. Example: Do you like milk?

notes.Are: Are goes with an adjective or -ing, not 'like'.
notes.Is: Is is for he/she/it with an adjective.

explain: Questions with he/she/it start with Does. Example: Does she swim?
can + verb (no -s, no to). Example: I can swim.

q: There are three ___ in the box.
explain: More than one: add -s. Example: one toy, three toys.

notes.a toy: A toy is one; we need three.

explain: We use the for one we can both see. Example: Look at the moon!

notes.a: A + elephant needs 'an', and here we point at one we see.
notes.an the: Don't use two little words together.
notes.these: These is for more than one.

explain: An before a, e, i, o, u sounds. Example: an egg, an apple.

notes.a: Orange starts with o, so an.
notes.two: Two needs a plural: two oranges.
notes.some: Some isn't used with one orange.

explain: My + noun: my bag. Mine stands alone: It's mine.

notes.me: Me is an object: Help me.
notes.I: I is a subject: I am.
notes.mine: Mine doesn't go before a noun.

q: Tom is a boy. ___ is nine.
explain: A boy = he. Example: He is my friend.

notes.It: It is for a thing or animal.

explain: In = inside. Example: The pen is in my bag.

notes.at: At is for a place or time: at school.
notes.of: Of shows a part: a cup of tea.
notes.to: To shows direction: go to school.

explain: In + season or month. Example: in summer, in June.

notes.on: On is for days: on Monday.
notes.at: At is for clock times: at 3 o'clock.
notes.of: Of doesn't go with seasons here.

explain: On + day. Example: on Sunday.

notes.in: In is for months: in May.
notes.at: At is for times: at six.

explain: At + clock time. Example: at 7 o'clock.

notes.in: In is for months and seasons.
notes.to: To isn't used with start times.

explain: He/she/it + verb + s for every day. Example: She eats toast.

q: I ___ swim. I'm scared of water.
explain: Can't = can not. Example: I can't sing.

notes.can: Can means you are able to.
notes.am not: Am not doesn't go with swim.

explain: Who asks about a person. Example: Who is he? — My dad.

notes.How: How asks about the way or feeling.

q: ___ is the park? — Next to the school.
explain: Where asks about a place. Example: Where is my hat?
How old…? asks about age. Example: How old is your cat?
These (more than one) + are. Example: These are my books.

notes.is: Is is for one: This is my shoe.

explain: Instructions use the plain verb. Example: Please sit down.
Don't + plain verb. Example: I don't eat fish.
Doesn't + plain verb. Example: He doesn't play tennis.

q: Is this ___ pencil? — Yes, it's Mia's.
explain: Her + noun shows a girl owns it. Example: her bike.

notes.she: She is a subject: She is tall.
notes.he: He is a boy, and a subject.

q: I'm ___ now. Can I have a sandwich?
explain: Feelings after I'm: hungry, tired, happy. Example: I'm hungry.

notes.thirsty: Thirsty means you want a drink.
notes.sleep: Sleep is a verb/noun; say sleepy.

explain: Let's + plain verb. Example: Let's play!

q: There ___ a dog in the garden.
explain: There is + one thing. Example: There is a cat.

notes.are: Are is for more than one.

q: There ___ two birds in the tree.
explain: There are + more than one. Example: There are three apples.
Some plurals are special: foot → feet. Example: my feet are cold.
Children is plural: are. Example: The children are happy.
He/she + is + job. Example: My dad is a cook.
Can + plain verb. Example: Can you sing?

q: It's ___ today. Let's go to the beach!
explain: Weather words: sunny, rainy, windy. Example: It's sunny.

notes.sun: Sun is the thing in the sky; the weather word is sunny.
notes.rain: Rain is a noun; say rainy, and the beach isn't fun then.
notes.snowy: Snowy weather isn't for the beach.

explain: I + plain verb for habits. Example: I wash my face.
After a verb use him/her/me. Example: I like her.

notes.he: He is a subject, not after a verb.

explain: Some + plural. Example: some sweets.

notes.one: One needs a singular: one apple.

explain: Ben and I = we → are. Example: Sam and I are twins.

notes.am: Am is only for I alone.

explain: What are you doing? asks about now. Example: What are you eating?
Is + -ing for now. Example: He is singing.

notes.draws: Draws is for every day, not now.

explain: He/she/it has. Example: My dog has big ears.
They have got… Example: We have got a car.
Has she got…? Example: Has he got a bike?

q: How many ___ are in your class?
explain: Child → children (special plural). Example: three children.

q: Two ___ are swimming in the pond.
explain: Fish usually stays the same for more than one. Example: one fish, five fish.

notes.fishes: Fishes is rare; kids' English says fish.

explain: Flavours have no a/an. Example: I like strawberry jam.

notes.chocolates: Chocolates are sweets, not a flavour.

explain: Socks (plural) + are. Example: Where are my shoes?
I am + age. Example: I am nine.

notes.have: In English we don't 'have' an age.

q: Is it a cat? — No, it ___.
explain: Short answer: No, it isn't. Example: Is it big? — No, it isn't.

q: Do you like pizza? — Yes, I ___.
explain: Short answer to Do…? : Yes, I do. Example: Do you swim? — Yes, I do.

notes.like: We don't repeat the verb in short answers.

explain: Short answer to Can…? : Yes, I can.

q: ___ are you? — I'm fine, thank you.
explain: How are you? asks how someone feels.
What time is it? asks the clock time.
What colour…? Example: What colour are your eyes?
On = on top of. Example: The cup is on the desk.

notes.at: At is for places like at school.

explain: Under = below. Example: The cat is under the bed.
Between + two people/things. Example: The shop is between the bank and the park.

notes.behind of: We say behind, not behind of.

explain: Is + -ing for now. Example: She is reading now.

notes.watches: Watches is for every day, not now.

explain: I + plain verb for every day. Example: I play football on Fridays.
Look! = now, so is + -ing. Example: Look! He's dancing!

notes.rains: Rains is for usually, not now.

explain: He/she/it + -s. Example: My dog likes bones.

notes.liking: Liking needs is, and we don't use it for likes.

explain: We have + lesson. Example: We have maths today.

notes.are: Are doesn't go with a lesson.

explain: Adjective after is: The apple is red.
Adjective before the noun: a black cat.

notes.cat black: The adjective goes first in English.

explain: Can + plain verb. Example: He can jump.

notes.ran: Ran is past; after can use run.

explain: Instructions start with the plain verb. Example: Close your books.
Don't + plain verb. Example: Don't run!
Short adjective + -er + than. Example: A dog is bigger than a cat.

notes.tallest: Tallest is for three or more.

explain: His + noun for a boy's thing. Example: his hat.
One thing + has. Example: The car has four wheels.

notes.are: Are is for more than one.

explain: Listen! = now; birds (plural) + are + -ing.
I don't + verb. Example: I don't like rain.

notes.am not: Am not doesn't go with like.

explain: Are you + adjective? Example: Are you cold?

notes.Do: Do doesn't go with an adjective.

q: My grandma ___ in a small village.
explain: He/she + -s for every day. Example: He lives in Tokyo.
Who + verb + what: I have a red bike.
She + is + who she is.
We + play + where.

answer: The cat is under the table.
explain: Thing + is + where it is.
Questions start with Do: Do you like…?
can + verb: He can swim.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: With he/she/it we say has: She has a cat.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: With I we say am: I am seven.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: With they/we/you we say are: They are my friends.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: With he/she/it add -s: He likes pizza.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: More than one: add -s. One cat, two cats.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: Use an before a, e, i, o, u sounds; dog starts with d, so a dog.

q: Fill the gaps with the words.
explain: I have; she is.

q: Fill the gaps with the words.
text: There ___ a dog. It ___ a long tail.
explain: There is one dog; it has a tail.

q: Fill the gaps with the words.
explain: We go (no -s); travel by bus.

q: Fill the gaps with the words.
explain: She drinks (+s); in the morning.
